messages:
jordan: Heads up — LensPay (customer) started seeing a flood of 429s ~30m after the rate-config push. Rollout was at 30% for the new rate policy. They also reported a sudden billing jump. Logs attached below. :worried:

maya: Copy, looking now. Which route/service? Any sample request IDs? :eyes:

jordan: Route is /v1/generate (rdx-small). Sample request id: 4f3a9b2c. Ingress shows a bunch of short retries within 2s windows. Snippet:```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] req=4f3a9b2c status=200 latency=120ms tokens=24
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] req=4f3a9b2c retry=1 -> 429 rate_limit key=org:lenspay shard=use1
[2026-03-15T10:12:04Z] req=8b2d... status=429 reason=burst_exhausted
```

liam: Noted. The deploy changed the per-key burst window from 1s->5s and the bucket refill semantics slightly. That should increase tolerance, not decrease it, but I can see interaction with our prefix caching: if KV cache misses and many requests cold-start the same session, concurrent token accounting could hit a race and double-count bursts.

maya: Could explain billing uplift if retries are counted as new token usage before dedupe. Jordan — can you attach a compressed pcap or the edge-ingress logs for 10:11:30-10:13:00? Also confirm if LensPay is on Dedicated or Hosted.

jordan: They're on Hosted (standard tier). Uploading logs to the #s3 link: https://s3.redwoodinternal/tmp/lenspay-spike-0315.tar.gz.

carla: I'm going to pause the rollout for the new policy group that contains LensPay. Switching feature-flag rate_policy_v2 -> false for cohort:cohort-2026-03-15. Will post when the gate is flipped.

deploy-bot: rollback-request accepted. Initiating cohort pause. snapshot_id=cohort-2026-03-15-snap-01

liam: Thanks. Quick repro plan: 1) replicate with our internal e2e by hammering a single API key with small concurrency but tight inter-request gaps (0-50ms). 2) observe token-bucket accounting in the policy service. 3) re-run with a KV cache warm path. I can run (1) in 10m.

maya: Also add a billing query: check for double-counted tokens around those request IDs and check if retries were counted as separate charges. If so, we need a hotfix in billing service to de-duplicate within X seconds (maybe 1s) for identical request ids/hashes.

jordan: Customer Success (ana-cs) on the thread — Ana, we've paused rollout and asked for logs. You can tell LensPay we've paused and we're investigating; ETA ~90m for initial root cause.

ana-cs: thanks jordan — I'll message them and offer to waive spikes while we triage. Any mitigations we should tell them to try on their side?

liam: If they can reduce client-side retries and backoff aggressively (exponential) for 429s that will reduce immediate load. Also if they can batch smaller requests less frequently for 30m it will help.

maya: I started a quick audit: policy-service metrics show a transient window where concurrent accounting increments were not atomic across redis shards (race on reconciling concurrent requests -> temporary overdraw). Patch candidate is a small CAS around increment+check. I'll stage to canary-offline env and run our repro.

carla: Good. Once liam confirms repro, we coordinate a targeted patch rollout to policy-service and a rollback/flush plan. Notify support before flipping back.

jordan: Confirming we will not re-enable cohort until we have the patch or an explicit mitigation. I'll keep the customer updated.

deploy-bot: cohort pause completed at 2026-03-15T10:18:56Z.

maya: Repro running now with liam's script. If we see the double-count, we'll promote the CAS patch to canary and then a limited 5% rollout with tight alarms.

jordan: Thanks everyone — I'll file the follow-up ticket and link it here with postmortem notes once we have root cause. :thumbsup:
